title: String methods
description: Core string methods for slicing, splitting, searching, casing, trimming, and replacing — the daily-driver toolkit.

notes: Strings are IMMUTABLE — every method returns a new string; the original is unchanged.
replace with a plain string replaces only the FIRST match. Use a /pattern/g regex (or replaceAll) for every match.
indexOf returns -1 when not found; includes returns a boolean. Pick by what you actually need.

questions.explain: slice(7) starts at index 7 and runs to the end.
Plain-string replace swaps only the first match. Use /g or replaceAll for all.

options: Only if the string was declared with `let` (the binding is mutable)
Only when the string contains lowercase chars; otherwise it is a no-op AND mutates

exercises.prompt: Slice "World" from "Hello, World" and "Hello" from the same string.
Trim whitespace then split the CSV.

L3.prompt: Write `normalize(s)` that trims, lowercases, and replaces ALL whitespace runs with "-". Log `normalize("  Hello World  ")`.
hints: Use a /\s+/g regex to catch every whitespace run.
